[ In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy. It ensures you win exactly when the price (second-highest bid) is below your value and maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. With only one round, there’s no benefit to shading or overbidding. My value is $31, so I bid exactly my value. ]

[ This is a sealed-bid second-price (Vickrey) auction. The dominant strategy is to bid my true value because my bid only determines whether I win, not the price I pay (which is the second-highest bid). Shading risks losing profitable wins without reducing price when I would win. With value $46, bidding 46 maximizes expected profit this round (and in the long run), winning whenever both others bid below 46 and paying the second-highest bid. No history to exploit; one round only. ]
